extraction.Name: Annie Desersa Bonser
extraction.Refused/Protested: Will Tackett called me by phone wanting to buy my land; this is the first I knew I had a patent and I told him I did not want. I told the Supt. at school that I did not want it; he was the one who gave it to me, it having been mailed to him to give to me.
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: Mortgaged and sold. Borrowed $550 from Walcott and Walcott. I sold it.
extraction.Buyer: Sold for $2200.00, paid by notes due every six months. Full amount paid. Buyer name not stated.
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: It was worth a whole lot more. I had to pay taxes and I was single at that time, and could not do it, therefore sold it.
extraction.NOTES: Received patent in 1918 at Genoa, Nebraska, at school, received by mail. Did not make application for patent. Did not remember signing a receipt for it. Has four children. Was single at time of sale. Not satisfied with the sale — land was worth more. Notarized April 9, 1929, before E. E. McKean.
